title: What is known about 1RB1LD_0RC1LE_1RD0LA_1RE0RF_1LF0LC_---1LB
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_0RC1LE_1RD0LA_1RE0RF_1LF0LC_---1LB.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. One round of a phase is proved in Lean for all sizes (round in lean/Rules.lean), and so are half a round for any left part and three shift rules. The conversions between phases go through several gadgets and are only described from simulation.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 37,049 cells have been visited and 35,963 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.07).

claims.title: One round of a phase
claims.text: From state A at the left end of 1 0 0 b c b^(k+2) 0 0 1^m (b = 1^6 0, c = 1^5 0) the machine reaches state A at the left end of 1 0 0 b c b^(k+1) 0 0 1^(m+10) in 80k + 307 steps, for every k, m and every tape to the right.

claims.title: Half a round, and the sweeps
claims.text: For any left part L, L 1 1 1 0 C> (1110111)^(n+1) 1 1 1 0 0 0 1^m reaches L A> 1 0 0 1^6 (0111111)^n 0 0 0 1^(m+5) (zig); three shift rules cross runs of 7-cell words.

claims.title: Phases and conversions
claims.text: When a run b^k is used up, the block of 1s to its right is cut into copies of c (for example 1^40215 became c^6703 at step 1,046,735,917). The c's are then turned into b's and 1s (here b^3351 and 1^16752), and the next phase starts. Large conversions were seen with c^94, c^151, c^343, c^638, c^1064, c^2338, c^6703 and c^9773 (the last at step 1,834,926,828). The left end runs through several different gadgets on the way, and these control which conversion happens.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The halting transition is F0, and F is entered only from E reading a 0 (1LF), so a halt needs E to read a 0 with a 0 to its left. A round cannot do that, so a halt could only come during a conversion. The conversions have not been reduced to a map.

check: gcc -O2 -o tok holdouts/1RB1LD_0RC1LE_1RD0LA_1RE0RF_1LF0LC_---1LB/c/tok.c && ./tok 1RB1LD_0RC1LE_1RD0LA_1RE0RF_1LF0LC_---1LB 100000000 at A L b=1111110,c=111110 1000000

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This machine is a nested counter. In each round one 7-cell word b turns into ten 1s (a Lean theorem for all sizes). When a run of b's is used up, the 1s are cut back into words and a new, longer phase starts. The way it is cut depends on a small gadget at the left end, and that part is not worked out.

facts.text: One round of a phase, proved for all counts.
The largest conversion seen, at step 1.8·10<sup>9</sup>.
No halt in the C simulator.

sections.heading: One b becomes ten 1s
html: With b = 1^6 0 and c = 1^5 0, the tape at the left end often reads 1 0 0 b c b^k 0 0 1^m .... The head starts in state A at the left end and zigzags twice across the run of b's. Each crossing re-encodes the run in another 7-cell word (0111111, 1110111, 1101111). The head comes back with b^(k-1) 0 0 1^(m+10), and the tape is three cells wider. This is the theorem round (80k + 147 steps for a run of k), for every k, m and every tape to the right; zig is half of it, for any left part.

sections.heading: Phases and conversions
html:
A run b^k next to a block 1^m is used up in k rounds and leaves 1^(m+10k). The machine then cuts that block back into words. For example, around step 1.05·109, 1^40215 became c^6703, and the c's then became b^3351 0 0 1^16752: a new run and a new block, and the next phase. Deeper in the tape there are further runs and blocks (for instance b^1788 0 0 1^8934 at step 6.6·108), so the counter is nested. The left end runs through several gadgets (1 0 0 b c, 1 0^6 c 0 0 c, 1 0^4 b 1^3 b c, ...), and which conversion follows depends on them and on residues of the block lengths: this is the Collatz-like part.

Large conversions seen so far: c^94, c^151, c^343, c^638, c^1064, c^2338, c^6703, c^9773 (step 1,834,926,828).

sections.heading: Where a halt would have to come from
html: The only halting transition is F on a 0. F is entered only from E reading a 0, so a halt needs 0 0 with E arriving on the right-hand 0. The proved round never does that, so a halt could only come during a conversion. The next step is to list the gadgets and prove each conversion with symtm, which gives a map on the counts that can then be iterated (see the README).

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.07).
After 109 steps the tape spans 37,049 cells (27,805 left of the start, 259 right), with a density of 1s of 0.971.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Words b = 1^6 0 and c = 1^5 0. In each round one b at the end of a run b^k becomes ten 1s of the block 1^m to its right (proved in Lean); when the run is empty the block 1^m is cut back into about m/6 copies of c and those into b's and 1s again, through several gadgets at the left end; the phase lengths grow irregularly.
